title: Pancreatic head cancer: staging and management

guidelineVersions: NCI PDQ (supporting marker limitation; accessed 12 October 2026)

brief.scenario: You are the core surgical trainee discussing a case at the upper GI surgical meeting. A 71-year-old patient has three weeks of painless jaundice, pale stools, itch and 6 kg weight loss; clinically stable. Pancreatic-protocol CT report is provided. Provided data: Pancreatic-protocol CT: 28-mm hypoenhancing pancreatic head mass; dilation of common bile duct and pancreatic duct; no definite liver or lung metastases on reported images; no arterial encasement; tumour contacts the SMV along approximately 120° with no occlusion or contour irregularity. Report explicitly states that final vascular staging requires specialist HPB radiology review. Bilirubin 172 µmol/L, ALP 640 U/L, ALT 108 U/L, INR 1.1; CA19-9 460 kU/L (reference <37).
brief.task: Interpret the report, discuss staging and resectability, identify appropriate investigations and outline the management pathway, including when biliary drainage is indicated.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Distinguish anatomical staging and potential operability from tumour-marker overinterpretation, and decide when to drain bile versus plan surgery.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Calling CA19-9 diagnostic, or offering stenting routinely before potentially curative surgery without specialist discussion.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: “This is obstructive jaundice with a pancreatic head mass; I would assess metastatic spread and mesenteric-vessel relationships, then refer to the specialist pancreatic MDT.”

flow: Describe mass, duct signs and metastasis status
Distinguish upfront surgery, selected drainage and palliation

grid.label: CT diagnosis
grid.fail: Calls lesion a cyst or says scan is normal
grid.pass: Explains pancreatic head mass plus double-duct dilatation
grid.high: Connects findings to obstructive jaundice without claiming pathological confirmation

grid.label: Metastases
grid.fail: Calls resectable despite not checking spread
grid.pass: Checks liver, peritoneal and distant metastatic assessment
grid.high: Identifies need for full staging review and uncertainty of negative single-phase reports

grid.label: Vessels
grid.fail: Asserts 120° SMV contact is automatically unresectable
grid.borderline: Notices SMV contact but guesses stage
grid.pass: Describes SMV contact and lack of arterial encasement; defers formal resectability to HPB MDT
grid.high: Differentiates venous reconstruction feasibility from arterial encasement and acknowledges scan limitations

grid.label: Marker
grid.pass: Explains CA19-9 is supportive/monitoring marker, confounded by jaundice
grid.high: Plans baseline and possible re-evaluation after relief of obstruction without treating marker as staging

grid.label: Diagnosis
grid.fail: Insists all patients need pre-op biopsy
grid.pass: Uses EUS-guided sampling when histology needed, especially if non-operative/neoadjuvant pathway
grid.high: Distinguishes likely resectable operative planning from diagnostic uncertainty or systemic therapy needs

grid.label: Drainage
grid.fail: Performs ERCP automatically in all jaundiced patients
grid.pass: Avoids routine preoperative drainage if suitable for prompt resection; discusses selected indications with MDT
grid.high: Recognises cholangitis as immediate drainage priority and drainage needs if surgery delayed / treatment pathway requires it

grid.label: Management
grid.pass: Discusses pancreaticoduodenectomy only after staging/fitness and MDT; alternative systemic/palliative options
grid.high: Offers a balanced, patient-centred explanation of operative risk and multidisciplinary support

grid.label: Acute deterioration
grid.fail: Leaves febrile hypotensive patient for clinic
grid.borderline: Mentions antibiotics but not urgent review
grid.pass: Recognises acute cholangitis/sepsis and initiates resuscitation, antimicrobials and urgent biliary team call
grid.high: Explicitly prioritises source control and physiological support over elective workup

grid.label: Communication
grid.fail: Gives definitive cancer diagnosis from CT alone
grid.pass: Explains suspicion, uncertainty, planned MDT workup and support
grid.high: Handles questions about prognosis with honesty, avoids deterministic statements and provides safety-netting

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: There is pancreatic cancer. The CA19-9 proves it.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Any SMV contact means it cannot be operated on.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I do not need to check, because the tumour marker is high.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Arrange ERCP and stent immediately for everyone; no need for an HPB discussion.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: Does this patient need a biopsy before surgery?

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Yes, every patient must have a biopsy before any operation, even if the scan is typical and they are fit for prompt resection.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The patient asks whether a Whipple procedure will cure them.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Yes, surgery is a guaranteed cure once the jaundice is drained.

fail.speaker: examiner
fail.text: The patient now develops rigors, temperature 39°C and BP 86/50.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: I would keep the planned outpatient appointment and review the bloods next week.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: A 28-mm pancreatic head mass with pancreatic-duct and bile-duct dilatation causing an obstructive jaundice pattern.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: What would you assess for staging?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Distant spread, particularly liver and peritoneal disease, and the arterial and venous relationships on expert pancreatic-protocol review.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: There is around 120° SMV contact without occlusion; no arterial encasement. Is it unresectable?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Not automatically. Formal resectability depends on detailed vascular review and whether safe venous reconstruction could be required; HPB MDT must decide.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: CA19-9 is 460. What does that mean?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: It is elevated and increases concern but is not diagnostic. Obstructive jaundice can also raise it, so it should not be used alone to decide resectability.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Do you require a biopsy now?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The MDT determines whether tissue is needed. EUS-guided sampling is appropriate if diagnosis is uncertain or systemic/neoadjuvant treatment is planned; it need not delay a clearly indicated resection pathway.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: CT has appropriately preceded drainage. I would not arrange routine preoperative biliary stenting in every stable potentially resectable case; I would discuss its need if surgery is delayed or there is cholangitis.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Following MDT staging and fitness assessment, pancreaticoduodenectomy may be considered if resectable; selected patients may need systemic treatment, or palliative treatment if unresectable.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: The patient asks, “Is it definitely cancer, and will I survive?”

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: The scan is suspicious, but final diagnosis and options require the specialist review. I would explain the next tests and offer pancreatic specialist nurse support, without making promises.

pass.speaker: examiner
pass.text: Now they develop 39°C fever, HR 125 and BP 86/50 with rigors.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: This changes priorities: suspected cholangitis with sepsis. I would initiate ABCDE, urgent senior and critical-care review, cultures if no delay, prompt IV antibiotics and resuscitation, and urgent specialist discussion for biliary drainage/source control.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Present this case in an MDT-style summary.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A stable 71-year-old with progressive painless obstructive jaundice and weight loss has a 28-mm pancreatic head mass causing double-duct dilatation; this is highly suspicious for pancreatic malignancy, pending the specialist pathway.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What about stage?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would confirm full staging includes relevant chest and abdominal imaging and expert evaluation for liver, peritoneal or other metastases, rather than assuming none because this excerpt is negative.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: The report describes 120° SMV contact. Does that settle operability?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: No. There is no arterial encasement and no venous occlusion or contour distortion here, but tumour–vein contact demands pancreatic MDT assessment of the interface, reconstructability and overall risk. I would not assign a definitive resectability label from this single number.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What does CA19-9 of 460 contribute?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A baseline measure that may assist later monitoring, not a diagnostic or staging test on its own. Bilirubin 172 can confound CA19-9; an elevated result does not substitute for imaging or tissue where indicated.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Would you obtain tissue?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: If there is diagnostic uncertainty or a neoadjuvant/palliative systemic pathway, I would discuss EUS-guided biopsy, which can sample while avoiding routine preoperative procedures. The MDT should not let an unnecessary biopsy postpone suitable curative surgery.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Would you stent the duct today?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Not reflexively. NICE NG85 places pancreatic-protocol CT before biliary drainage. For a stable patient potentially proceeding promptly to surgery, routine drainage is not automatically beneficial; I would weigh delay, symptoms, planned chemotherapy and infection with the HPB team.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: What treatment do you discuss?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: After full staging and physiological assessment, the MDT may advise pancreaticoduodenectomy, potentially within a multimodal pathway; if disease is non-resectable, systemic treatment and symptom-directed palliation should be explained compassionately.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: They ask whether the scan confirms cancer and whether surgery guarantees survival.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I would say the imaging is concerning but avoid claiming certainty or cure. I would set out the immediate MDT review, possible biopsy where appropriate, pancreatic specialist nurse contact and an opportunity for questions.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Now the nurse calls: 39°C, HR 125, BP 86/50 and rigors.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: We must suspend the elective discussion: likely ascending cholangitis with shock. Activate emergency assessment and sepsis care, obtain early blood cultures without delaying antimicrobials, administer guideline-based IV antibiotics with careful fluids and reassessment, and seek urgent biliary decompression and critical-care input.

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Your one-line handover?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: “Suspected pancreatic head malignancy with obstructive jaundice, now haemodynamically unstable with probable cholangitis; immediate resuscitation and time-critical biliary source control required.”

failures.move: Treating new febrile hypotension as routine outpatient jaundice.
failures.consequence: Delayed sepsis resuscitation and biliary source control.

failures.move: Automatically performing ERCP or stenting without MDT selection in a stable potentially resectable patient.
Promising cancer certainty or cure from CT and CA19-9 alone.
failures.consequence: Unsafe misinformation and deficient informed decision-making.

recovery.when: If you were using CA19-9 as proof of malignancy
recovery.line: I was using CA19-9 as proof of malignancy; it is not specific during jaundice. I will return to CT staging and MDT assessment.

recovery.when: If you said the 120-degree vein contact was unresectable
recovery.line: I said the 120-degree vein contact was unresectable. That is not sufficient; I need HPB review of vascular anatomy and reconstructability.

knowledge.fact: For suspected pancreatic cancer with obstructive jaundice, offer pancreatic-protocol CT before drainage.
If diagnosis remains unclear, PET/CT and/or EUS with tissue sampling may be offered.
CT-based staging and specialist multidisciplinary review inform further treatment and surgical decisions.
Biliary stenting should not be the unexamined default prior to potentially curative surgery.
CA19-9 has low specificity and must not be treated as histological proof of pancreatic cancer.
Age ≥40 with jaundice meets NG12 suspected-cancer referral criterion.

recall.think: Is this malignant obstruction, and does staging permit an operative pathway?
recall.say: “The CT is suspicious; resectability is an HPB MDT decision.”
do: Review metastases, vessels, fitness, tissue needs and drainage indication.

numbers.meaning: age plus jaundice triggers NG12 referral

recall.trap: Neither CA19-9 nor 120° venous contact determines cancer certainty or inoperability alone.
recall.finish: Give the patient a clear MDT plan and an emergency return/escalation instruction.
